title: COMP 4537 · Lecture 3
subtitle: Why API servers exist, the four parts of a web API, GET vs POST, Postman, and REST's constraints with the microservice gateway
description: Lecture 3 of Amir Amintabar's COMP 4537: the review programs (var, let and const scope, the A/B/C hoisting scenarios, the 1 3 2 event-queue script) as predicts; why a monolithic web server that returns rendered HTML pages is a problem for other programs, told through the online movie store, IMDb scraping and the OMDb API server that returns JSON; the API as a documented contract; the anatomy of a web API (headers, data, endpoint, HTTP methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) shown on live requests to the app's echo endpoint; the full GET vs POST comparison table (cache, history, bookmark, the 2048-character URL, ASCII only, neither is secure); testing an API with Postman and httpbin; REST as an architectural style, microservices behind an API gateway, and the five RESTful constraints with their principle, benefit and example, plus Code-on-Demand. Ends with a 20-item mock quiz.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm weight
The midterm is 30 % of the course and covers lectures 1 to 6 in full plus the Node-to-MySQL part of lecture 7, so this lecture is roughly one seventh of the exam, about 10 to 15 %. Its facts reach the exam in all four question kinds: one-fact MCQs and true/false on the GET vs POST table and the four parts of a web API, what-prints items on the review programs, and short or medium answers on REST's five constraints and on GET vs POST. Learning Hub Quizzes 6 and 7 already asked which method can be bookmarked, which can carry a 1 GB request, whether GET is fine for credentials, which method edits a profile, and which GET/POST statement is false.
:::
